chunks: And it is narrated from ʿAlī ibn Mahziyār, who said:
I said to Abū Jaʿfar al-Thānī عليه السلام regarding His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He:
"By the night when it covers, and by the day when it shines forth."
and His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He:
and other similar verses. So he عليه السلام said:
"Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, swears by whatever He wills from His creation, and it is not for His creation to swear except by Him, Mighty and Majestic."

key_terms.إِلَّا بِهِ: except by Him, meaning only Allah may be invoked in an oath
key_terms.بِمَا يَشَاءُ: by whatever He wills, indicating Allah's unrestricted divine choice
key_terms.خَلْقِهِ: His creation, meaning created things over which Allah has authority
key_terms.لَيْسَ لِخَلْقِهِ: it is not for His creation, meaning humans do not share this prerogative
key_terms.وَاللَّيْلِ: the night, part of a Qur'anic divine oath
key_terms.وَالنَّجْمِ: the star, part of a Qur'anic divine oath

ai.seo_question: Can people swear by created things the way Allah does in the Qur'an?
ai.summary: This hadith explains that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, may swear by whatever He wills from among His creation in the Qur'an. Human beings, however, are not permitted to swear except by Allah, making this both a point of Qur'anic commentary and a legal ruling regarding oaths.
